items.desc: Hailing from La Rioja in Argentina, Juan Ibañez is part of a new generation of South American producers bringing fresh energy to the scene. His growing international profile has taken him across Europe, Asia and Latin America, while his productions continue to find an audience well beyond his native Argentina. In 2026, he collaborated on ‘Auralis’, a richly textured progressive house cut featured on the This Is Balance Croatia 2026 compilation. Beyond the studio, Ibañez is also the founder of Desierto, an event platform dedicated to developing electronic music culture in northern Argentina. O…
items.title: Balance Selections 389: Juan Ibañez

items.desc: The title track ‘Run For Cover’ taps into the wide-eyed escapism of the mid-’90s without slipping into nostalgia. Psychedelic details flicker across the drums like LED trails in a dark room, while a restless walking bassline gives the whole thing a wonderfully physical pull. Elements drift in and out of focus, resisting an obvious genre tag while maintaining an easy, heads-down momentum. It’s progressive music in the literal sense: constantly moving, never particularly interested in announcing where it’s going next.
items.title: [PREVIEW] Nick Warren - Run For Cover

items.desc: On “Stupa”, the mood opens outward. There’s an unmistakable Balearic quality to its sun-warmed percussion and serrated bassline,a groove that immediately suggests open-air dancefloors and late-afternoon light. A woozy synth gradually sends proceedings into more narcotic territory, while soft vocal fragments, keyboard flourishes and flashes of guitar keep one foot planted somewhere recognisably human. Nothing is hurried or overplayed. Instead, Warren lets each element breathe, resulting in the kind of patient, transportive dance music that comes from knowing exactly how little you need to do.
items.title: [PREVIEW] Nick Warren - Stupa

items.desc: Colombian DJ NAJEYS has developed a sound rooted in the melodic and hypnotic strains of progressive house. With a background in vocals and percussion, she began exploring electronic music in 2016, developing an approach to DJing that balances driving rhythms, atmospheric textures and emotive melodies. A resident at Medellín’s Club Sonorama and winner of Colombia’s Best Progressive DJ award in 2022, NAJEYS has performed at major festivals across Colombia, Mexico, Curaçao and Argentina. She next opens for Martin Garrix at Medellín’s Davi Arena on December 5th, with new music also on the horizon…
items.title: Balance Selections 388: NAJEYS

items.desc: Alej Ch is a producer and DJ working across organic, deep and progressive house. His releases have appeared on labels including Warpp, Songuara and Melody of the Soul. A self-taught musician, he came to production through piano and guitar before developing a sound built around intricate melodies and dramatic flourishes. His recent work sits comfortably between the more organic end of house and deeper, club-focused territory. On this Balance Selections mix, the Greek producer delivers a polished 60-minute session that marks him as one to watch. Featuring tracks from Ezequiel Arias, Redspace, M…
items.title: Balance Selections 385: Alej Ch

items.desc: On the optimistic ‘Hikari’, a rolling bassline drives the track forward with an infectious low-end pulse that will be difficult to ignore on the dancefloor. A stretched vocal sample drifts across uplifting melodic keys, creating a genuine feeling of space and freedom. In Japanese, hikari means “light”, a word often associated with hope, positivity and clarity. It’s a fitting title for a track that channels those exact qualities.
items.title: [PREVIEW] D-SHIFT - Hikari

items.desc: Lead cut ‘Find a Way’ draws on the genre’s classic foundations, built around a warm vocal sample and bubbling synths. A beautifully measured breakdown opens the track up, as melodic layers gather around the vocal before the groove locks back into place. It’s A-grade dancefloor material, with enough presence to become the defining moment of a set. @drunkenkongjp
items.title: [PREVIEW] D-SHIFT - Find A Way
